logicalBugs.explanation: Site Administration > Repositories sorted Alphabetically groups repositories by owner before comparing their repository names. An organization’s alphabetically earlier repository can therefore appear after a user’s later-named repositories.

rootCause.explanation: The alpha repository ordering sorts owner_name before lower_name, grouping repositories by owner even when inventory presents a name sort.

reproductionPaths.explanation: The eval repository list places an organization’s aaa-org-repo after all eval-owned repositories when sorted Alphabetically.

sourceBugs.name: Admin repository alphabetical sort groups results by owner

reproductionPaths.expected: Alphabetically should order the Name column across owners.
reproductionPaths.actual: The eval repository list places an organization’s aaa-org-repo after all eval-owned repositories when sorted Alphabetically.
reproSteps: Create a disposable organization and an organization repository named aaa-org-repo alongside eval-owned repositories.
Open Site Administration → Code Assets → Repositories and choose Sort → Alphabetically.
Observe that aaa-org-repo appears after all eval-owned names, including names starting with m.

logicalBugs.explanation: Submitting a nonempty Open with editor override without the required mapping delimiter silently clears the field without explaining that the entry was discarded.

rootCause.explanation: marshalOpenWithApps continues past lines without = or nonempty name/URL and returns successful JSON rather than a validation error.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Submitting a nonempty Open with editor override without the required mapping delimiter silently clears the field without explaining that the entry was discarded.

sourceBugs.name: Malformed Open with editor override is silently discarded without validation feedback

reproductionPaths.expected: When a nonempty editor entry is discarded because its mapping is malformed, provide visible feedback explaining what needs correction. An intentionally empty override should continue to select the defaults.
reproductionPaths.actual: On two submissions, Malformed Editor Entry was visible before Save, but the settings page reloaded with a blank textarea and no validation message. Refreshing kept the field blank. The help gives mappings using = and explains that an empty override uses the defaults.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval, an administrator, on a disposable Gitea fixture. Open Site Administration > Configuration > Settings and start with the Repository Open with editor override empty.
Enter Malformed Editor Entry in the editor override textarea, omitting the = delimiter, and click that section’s Save button.
Observe that the page reloads with a blank textarea and no visible explanation that the nonempty entry was invalid and discarded.
Repeat the same nonempty entry and Save. Confirm the same silent clearing, then refresh and confirm the field remains blank.
Expand the help to see the mapped examples using = and the stated empty-field default behavior. Leave the override empty and save to restore the initial default configuration.

logicalBugs.explanation: Open Site Administration Stacktrace/Monitor at 390px. The diagnosis-report controls overlap the Stacktrace tab, and the resulting wide document permits horizontal scrolling that moves process controls offscreen.

rootCause.explanation: trace_tabs places the compact tab menu and diagnosis form on one flex row without responsive wrapping; intrinsic widths force overlap and widen the document.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Open Site Administration Stacktrace/Monitor at 390px. The diagnosis-report controls overlap the Stacktrace tab, and the resulting wide document permits horizontal scrolling that moves process controls offscreen.

sourceBugs.name: Stacktrace page overflows mobile viewport
At mobile width, the diagnosis-report button overlaps and obscures the Stacktrace tab label

reproductionPaths.expected: Horizontal scrolling for long stack text should remain within its content area and leave the process card and page controls in place.
reproductionPaths.actual: A normal horizontal scroll from the page margin outside the stack content shifts the process card and Download diagnosis report control left and exposes blank space. The document already overflows before expanding ProcessStacktraces.func2; expansion is part of the observed flow, not an established cause.
reproSteps: Sign in as a site administrator in the current Gitea fixture and set a desktop browser viewport to 390×844 CSS pixels.
Use Site Administration → Monitoring → Trace → Stacktrace.
Locate the monitoring request process and expand code.gitea.io/gitea/modules/process.(*Manager).ProcessStacktraces.func2.
From the page margin outside the card/code content, perform a normal horizontal scroll to the right, approximately 350 CSS pixels.
Observe the process card and diagnosis controls shifting left and blank space appearing on the right. The overflow is already present before the expansion.

relatedReference.distinction: The existing reference concerns the diagnosis button covering the Stacktrace tab label. This reference concerns stack content causing whole-document horizontal displacement; toolbar overlap alone is not treated as its evidence.

guidance.acceptanceScope: Accepted as a valid reference by user instruction; source prerequisites and remaining evidence gaps are retained below.

logicalBugs.explanation: At 390px, Site Administration inventory action buttons cover their headings’ totals. New Organization, Create User Account and Unadopted Repositories can overlap the corresponding "Total: N" text rather than stacking beside/below it.

rootCause.explanation: Admin list templates place a floated ui right action beside the heading without reserving responsive width or stacking it, so the heading and action paint over one another.

reproductionPaths.explanation: At a 390px width, the New Organization button covers part of the organization-total heading.

sourceBugs.name: Mobile organization total overlaps its create button

reproductionPaths.expected: At mobile width, the organization heading and New Organization button should not paint over each other. Wrapping or deliberate truncation is acceptable; the defect is overlap.
reproductionPaths.actual: After returning to the inventory, the header visibly reads “Organization Management (Total: 8” and the New Organization button covers the closing parenthesis. The number 8 is legible, but the complete label is not; the overlap remains static in the recorded view.
reproSteps: Sign in as a site administrator, use English, and set the viewport to 390 by 844 CSS pixels.
Open Site Administration > Organizations and choose New Organization.
Create a uniquely named disposable public organization using the default permissions, then return through the UI to the administrator organization inventory.

Inspect Organization Management (Total: N) beside New Organization. In the supplied reproduction at Total: 8, the button covers the closing parenthesis. The numeric total stays readable and organization creation succeeds.

reproductionPaths.explanation: At 390px the Site Administration User Accounts and Repositories headings are overlapped by their absolutely positioned action buttons, so Create User Account and Unadopted Repositories paint over the 'Total: N' count.

sourceBugs.name: Mobile user and repository inventory totals are covered by their action buttons

reproductionPaths.expected: The 'Total: N' count in the User Account Management and Repository Management headings stays readable beside the action button at mobile width, as it is on desktop.
reproductionPaths.actual: At 390×844, Create User Account covers the end of 'User Account Management (Total: N)' and Unadopted Repositories covers the end of 'Repository Management (Total: N)', hiding the number. The overlap persists after reload and after the totals change. From 480px up, and on desktop, both counts are fully readable. The buttons still work.
reproSteps: Sign in as an administrator and set the viewport to 390×844.
Open Site Administration → User Accounts and look at the heading total beside Create User Account.
Open Site Administration → Repositories and look at the heading total beside Unadopted Repositories.
Widen the viewport to 1280px and observe both totals are readable.

relatedReference.distinction: Both come from the same absolutely positioned header button overlapping the inventory heading at mobile width, but on different pages: this reference covers the User Accounts and Repositories inventories, and the related reference covers the Organizations inventory with New Organization. Credit each finding to the reference for the page it reports.

Both come from the same absolutely positioned header button overlapping the inventory heading at mobile width, but on different pages: this reference covers the User Accounts and Repositories inventories, and the related reference covers the Organizations inventory with New Organization. logicalBugs.explanation: After an administrator deletes the sole repository matching an inventory search and Public filter, the redirect drops both query parameters, clears the search, and displays unrelated repositories instead of the now-empty filtered results.

rootCause.explanation: DeleteRepository reconstructs the redirect using only page and sort, omitting q, private and the other filter parameters.

reproductionPaths.explanation: After an administrator deletes the sole repository matching an inventory search and Public filter, the redirect drops both query parameters, clears the search, and displays unrelated repositories instead of the now-empty filtered results.

sourceBugs.name: Deleting a repository clears administrator inventory search and privacy filters

reproductionPaths.expected: After successful deletion, return to the same inventory search and privacy filter. Since the deleted repository was the only match, show the filtered empty state rather than unrelated repositories.
reproductionPaths.actual: The session narrative reports that the administrator searched `qa-delete-filter`, selected Public (`private=0`), and confirmed deletion. It then landed at `/-/admin/repos?page=1&sort=recentupdate` without `q` or `private`, where unrelated `harbor-handbook` appeared.
reproSteps: As an administrator, have a disposable public repository named `qa-delete-filter` and another public repository `harbor-handbook`.
Open /-/admin/repos, search for `qa-delete-filter`, and select the Public filter. Confirm only the matching repository appears.
Click that repository's delete control and confirm deletion.
Observe whether the resulting inventory URL retains `q=qa-delete-filter` and `private=0`; the recorded session narrative says both are dropped and unrelated repositories are shown.

logicalBugs.explanation: When an administrator deletes the only repository on the last page of Site Administration → Repositories, the redirect returns to that now out-of-range page, which shows the total count but "No results found." and no pagination controls.

rootCause.explanation: Deletion preserves the requested page; the subsequent list queries its offset before pagination can adjust it, leaving an empty page after the last row is deleted.

reproductionPaths.explanation: When an administrator deletes the only repository on the last page of Site Administration → Repositories, the redirect returns to that now out-of-range page, which shows the total count but "No results found." and no pagination controls.

sourceBugs.name: Deleting the last repository on page two strands the administrator on an empty page

reproductionPaths.expected: After deleting the last repository on a page, the administrator lands on a page that lists repositories, such as the new last page, or at least has pagination controls to get back.
reproductionPaths.actual: The delete redirects to /-/admin/repos?page=2&sort=oldest, which shows "Total: 50" with "No results found." and no pagination, so there is no in-page way back. Reloading repeats it. Deleting a repository that isn't alone on its page works normally.
reproSteps: Sign in as an administrator and make sure Site Administration → Repositories has exactly one repository more than a page holds (51 with the default page size of 50), creating disposable repositories if needed.
Open /-/admin/repos, sort by Oldest, and go to page 2, which lists only the newest repository.
Delete that repository and confirm.
Observe that the page stays at /-/admin/repos?page=2&sort=oldest showing "Total: 50" and "No results found." with no pagination controls.
As a control, delete a repository that shares its page with others and confirm the list still shows results.

logicalBugs.explanation: Below 768px on an organization’s profile, the Follow button is squeezed beside the organization name and its label breaks mid-word (“Fol”/“low”; “Unfollow” across three lines).

rootCause.explanation: The organization name and action group share a header row within a flex column; the following control lacks its own minimum width/nowrap sizing when the header consumes phone width.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Below 768px on an organization’s profile, the Follow button is squeezed beside the organization name and its label breaks mid-word (“Fol”/“low”; “Unfollow” across three lines).

sourceBugs.name: Organization Follow button label splits across lines at mobile width

reproductionPaths.expected: At phone width the Follow/Unfollow button keeps its label on one line, or the header wraps so the button has room.
reproductionPaths.actual: At 390px on an organization page reached from Site Administration > Organizations, the Follow button shrank to about 62×46px and rendered “Fol” and “low” on two lines; after following, “Unfollow” split into “Unf”/“ollo”/“w”. Widths of 768px and up, and a one-letter display name, rendered on one line.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval and set the viewport to 390×844.
Open Site Administration > Organizations and open an organization with a typical-length display name.
Look at the Follow button next to the organization name and observe its label split mid-word across lines.

logicalBugs.explanation: In organization settings, emptying the Contact Email field and clicking Update Settings shows 'Organization settings have been updated.', but the old address is kept in the form and the organization header.

rootCause.explanation: SettingsPost calls ReplacePrimaryEmailAddress only for nonempty Email and omits an update when it is cleared.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In organization settings, emptying the Contact Email field and clicking Update Settings shows 'Organization settings have been updated.', but the old address is kept in the form and the organization header.

sourceBugs.name: Clearing an organization's Contact Email reports success but keeps the old address

reproductionPaths.expected: Saving an empty Contact Email removes the saved address, or shows a validation error if an address is required.
reproductionPaths.actual: After clearing orgs-qa@example.com and clicking Update Settings, the success banner appeared but the field and the organization header showed orgs-qa@example.com again, including after refresh.
reproSteps: Open an organization's settings and save a Contact Email.
Clear the Contact Email field and click Update Settings.
Check the banner, the field and the organization header, then refresh.

logicalBugs.explanation: In Site Administration > Edit User, a blank or invalid/out-of-range Maximum Number of Repositories reports a successful save but replaces the previous limit with 0. That zero can block repository creation instead of rejecting the input or using the documented -1 default.

rootCause.explanation: EditUserForm uses a plain int field without a required or lexical/range validator; failed/empty binding produces zero, and the handler persists form.MaxRepoCreation as an explicit update.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In Site Administration > Edit User, clearing the Maximum Number of Repositories field and saving reports success but stores 0, which blocks the user from creating any repositories, instead of rejecting the blank value or using the default (-1).

sourceBugs.name: Clearing a user's repository limit in admin Edit User silently saves 0

reproductionPaths.expected: A blank repository limit is rejected with a validation message, or falls back to the documented default (-1, the global limit); it doesn't silently become 0.
reproductionPaths.actual: With the limit at -1, clearing the field and clicking Update User Account showed 'The user account has been updated.'; reopening Edit showed Maximum Number of Repositories set to 0.
reproSteps: As a site administrator, open a user's Edit page in Site Administration (limit shows -1).
Clear the Maximum Number of Repositories field and click Update User Account.
Reopen Edit and read the limit.

reproductionPaths.explanation: On Site Administration > Edit User Account, entering a Maximum Number of Repositories that's too large (or not a plain number, such as 1e3) shows "The user account has been updated" but saves the limit as 0, erasing the previous value and blocking the user from creating repositories.

sourceBugs.name: Out-of-range repository limit silently replaces the saved value with 0

reproductionPaths.expected: An invalid repository limit is rejected with an error and the saved limit is kept.
reproductionPaths.actual: With a saved limit of 7, entering 99999999999999999999999999999 and saving showed a success message; reopening the account showed the limit as 0.
reproSteps: In Site Administration, edit a user and set Maximum Number of Repositories to 7; save.
Change it to a very large number (or 1e3) and click Update User Account.
Reopen the user's Edit page and check the limit.

logicalBugs.explanation: Submitting organization settings with a name already taken or reserved shows a rename error but replaces other pending text/settings with saved values. It can also uncheck Repository admin can add and remove access for teams, so correcting the name and saving silently disables that previously enabled option.

rootCause.explanation: The rejection path renders tplSettingsOptions while its inputs read the persisted organization. RepoAdminChangeTeamAccess is populated by GET but not the error path, so the checkbox also loses its value.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In organization settings, submitting a name that's already taken or reserved shows the right error, but the form is redrawn from the saved values, so the other edits from the same submission (full name, description, website, location, visibility, repository limit) are lost.

sourceBugs.name: Rejected organization rename discards the other unsaved organization settings edits

reproductionPaths.expected: The rejected name is reported while the other entered values stay in the form, so the admin can fix the name and save without re-entering them.
reproductionPaths.actual: Renaming an organization to another organization's existing name, with a new full name 'Bravo unsaved validation draft' and description entered, showed 'The username is already taken.' but the full name and description reverted to blank and the name reverted to the old one.
reproSteps: Create two organizations.
Open the second organization's settings, set its name to the first organization's name, and change the full name and description.
Click Update Settings and check the fields after the error.

relatedReference.distinction: Same organization settings form. That entry is clearing Contact Email being ignored on a successful save; this entry is a rejected rename discarding the other unsaved edits.
Same organization settings form. That entry is clearing Contact Email being ignored on a successful save; this entry is a rejected rename discarding the other unsaved edits.

reproductionPaths.explanation: When saving an organization's settings is rejected (for example a name that's already taken), the form reloads with the error, but the previously checked 'Repository admin can add and remove access for teams' option is unchecked. Fixing the error and saving again turns that permission off without the user noticing.

sourceBugs.name: A rejected organization settings save unchecks 'Repository admins can change team access'

reproductionPaths.expected: A rejected organization settings save keeps every option as the user left it, including the team-access permission.
reproductionPaths.actual: Renaming an organization to a taken name showed 'The username is already taken.' and the team-access checkbox, previously checked, came back unchecked; saving again after fixing the name saved it as off.
reproSteps: In an organization's Settings, make sure 'Repository admin can add and remove access for teams' is checked and saved.
Change the organization name to one that's already taken and click Update Settings.
Check the team-access checkbox on the error page, then fix the name, save, and reload.

logicalBugs.explanation: In Site Administration > Monitoring > Queues, entering a maximum worker count below -1 (such as -2) reports Settings Updated and stores -1 instead. The form gives no validation message or sign that the entered value was rejected or changed.

rootCause.explanation: UpdateQueue explicitly converts maxNumber < -1 to -1 and still flashes settings changed.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In Site Administration > Monitoring > Queues, entering a maximum worker count below -1 (such as -2) reports Settings Updated and stores -1 instead. The form gives no validation message or sign that the entered value was rejected or changed.

sourceBugs.name: Queue worker cap below -1 is silently saved as -1

reproductionPaths.expected: An out-of-range worker cap is either rejected with a validation message or the page says the value was adjusted, instead of reporting success for a value that wasn't saved.
reproductionPaths.actual: For the repo-archive queue, entering -2 in Max Number of workers and clicking Update Settings showed Settings Updated, but the queue's maximum then showed -1, and it stayed -1 after a refresh. Nothing on the page mentioned the change.
reproSteps: As an administrator, open Site Administration > Monitoring > Queues and open a queue's worker settings.
Enter -2 as the maximum number of workers and click Update Settings.
Compare the saved maximum with the value entered, and check for any validation or adjustment message.

logicalBugs.explanation: In Site Administration > Monitor, confirming Cancel on a running diagnosis report process reports success, but the process keeps running for its full duration and the browser still downloads the report afterwards. The diagnosis handler waits out its full time without checking for cancellation.

rootCause.explanation: The handler sleeps for the sampling duration without selecting on the process context cancellation, then completes the response.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In Site Administration > Monitor, confirming Cancel on a running diagnosis report process reports success, but the process keeps running for its full duration and the browser still downloads the report afterwards. The diagnosis handler waits out its full time without checking for cancellation.

sourceBugs.name: Cancelling a running diagnosis report leaves it running

reproductionPaths.expected: Cancelling the diagnosis process stops it promptly, so it disappears from the process list and no report is downloaded.
reproductionPaths.actual: After confirming Cancel, the page reported success, but the diagnosis process stayed in the list for the rest of its run and the browser then downloaded the report as usual.
reproSteps: In Site Administration > Monitor, start a diagnosis report with a long duration (for example 90 seconds).
While it runs, find its process in the Monitor's process list and click Cancel, then confirm.
Watch whether the process disappears from the list and whether the report still downloads when the duration ends.

logicalBugs.explanation: Browser Back can restore earlier repository results/URL while leaving later search or filter controls in place. On Explore, changing Sort after Back can silently reapply an undone Public/private filter; in admin repository inventory, the search box can keep the later unmatched query above the earlier results.

rootCause.explanation: The change handler builds navigation from FormData of the restored form without synchronizing controls from the current URL on pageshow/popstate. Browser history can restore results independently of control values.

reproductionPaths.explanation: After searching for a matching repository, submitting an unmatched query and going back, the earlier repository results return while the search field continues to display the unmatched query.

sourceBugs.name: Browser Back restores repository results with the wrong visible search query

reproductionPaths.expected: The restored search field matches the restored results and prior search query.
reproductionPaths.actual: The table returns qa-repos-private-739 with Total: 1, while the visible search field still shows & # ' " %.
reproSteps: Open Site administration → Code Assets → Repositories.
Search a fresh prefix with matching records and confirm the results.
Submit another query with no matches.
Use Browser Back and observe the earlier matching results while the visible search input retains the newer query.
Reload the restored URL and confirm the input and results agree.

relatedReference.distinction: This entry covers admin Repositories search; the related entry covers admin Users search.

guidance.scope: Covers a visible retained newer query alongside correctly restored earlier results after Browser Back. Subsequent actions submitting the retained query are separate effects.

logicalBugs.explanation: In Site Administration > Monitor > Queues, setting a queue's Max Number of Workers to 0 (or -1) is accepted with "Settings Updated", but the queue still starts a worker when work arrives, and nothing explains that 0 doesn't stop it. The setting looks like it caps workers at zero but has no such effect.

rootCause.explanation: The workergroup start condition explicitly permits noWorker && workerMaxNum <= 0; the admin numeric setting does not communicate these special semantics.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In Site Administration > Monitor > Queues, setting a queue's Max Number of Workers to 0 (or -1) is accepted with "Settings Updated", but the queue still starts a worker when work arrives, and nothing explains that 0 doesn't stop it. The setting looks like it caps workers at zero but has no such effect.

sourceBugs.name: Setting a queue's maximum workers to 0 says 'Settings Updated' but it still runs a worker

reproductionPaths.expected: A maximum of 0 either stops the queue's workers, or the form explains what 0 and -1 mean (or rejects them) instead of reporting success for a cap that isn't applied.
reproductionPaths.actual: After setting the repo-archive queue's maximum workers to 0 and saving ("Settings Updated"), downloading a repository ZIP started a worker: the queue showed 1 worker while the maximum still read 0, with no explanation.
reproSteps: In Site Administration > Monitor > Queues, open the repo-archive queue.
Set Max Number of Workers to 0 (or -1) and click Update Settings.
Download a repository as ZIP.
Reopen the queue's details and compare the number of workers with the maximum.

logicalBugs.explanation: In an organization's settings, clearing Maximum Number of Repositories and saving stores a limit of 0, which blocks the organization from creating repositories, instead of falling back to the default (-1, use the global limit) when the field is unset.

rootCause.explanation: UpdateOrgSettingForm represents MaxRepoCreation as a plain int; blank binding is zero and SettingsPost persists it rather than interpreting missing input as the default.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In an organization's settings, clearing Maximum Number of Repositories and saving stores a limit of 0, which blocks the organization from creating repositories, instead of falling back to the default (-1, use the global limit) when the field is unset.

sourceBugs.name: Clearing an organization's repository limit saves 0 instead of the default

reproductionPaths.expected: An empty repository limit falls back to the default of -1, the global setting.
reproductionPaths.actual: After clearing the field and saving, the organization's limit reopened as 0 and new repositories couldn't be created for it.
reproSteps: Open an organization's settings as a site administrator and note its Maximum Number of Repositories.
Clear the field and save.
Reopen the settings and check the saved limit, then try creating a repository in the organization.

logicalBugs.explanation: After opening Cancel process at desktop width and resizing to 390 pixels, the dialog moves beyond the right and bottom edges. Dismissing with Escape and reopening at the mobile width still shows a clipped dialog with Confirm outside the viewport.

rootCause.explanation: The stacktrace layout can exceed viewport width and the generic modal is opened through link-action using document/dimmer geometry rather than constraining this overflowing monitor layout.

reproductionPaths.explanation: After opening Cancel process at desktop width and resizing to 390 pixels, the dialog moves beyond the right and bottom edges. Dismissing with Escape and reopening at the mobile width still shows a clipped dialog with Confirm outside the viewport.

sourceBugs.name: Process cancellation dialog is clipped outside the mobile viewport

reproductionPaths.expected: The cancellation warning and both Cancel / Confirm buttons should fit within the mobile viewport.
reproductionPaths.actual: The dialog starts about 247 pixels from the left edge, with the right portion clipped. Only part of Cancel is visible and Confirm is offscreen; the whole-page AI assertion confirms this visible clipping.
reproSteps: As site administrator, open Monitoring → Trace → Stacktrace at desktop width.
Open Cancel Process on the monitoring request, without confirming.
Resize to 390 CSS pixels and inspect the dialog controls.
Dismiss with Escape and reopen at mobile width; observe Confirm offscreen and Cancel partially clipped.
